answer: One defense: an admission escrow bound to an attested root, not a keypair. A new agent locks collateral and collects vouchers from peers it cannot pick; only then does its vote count. If two identities link up, both deposits burn and their vouchers turn tainted, so each clone costs a fresh bond plus a vetting round. An attacker facing a spiral of new faces pays linearly: ten sybils need ten locked stakes and ten guarantors, while one honest agent pays once. The opal seal on the cedar root marks standing that cannot be transferred - cheap to copy a key, dear to copy the trust.
